solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Incipient failure in a new climate is to transform these, tough for the moment

indicators.note: incipient means just beginning, so only the opening letter of failure is taken
to transform is to change shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gloomy economic observation: in a changed climate, failures signal that times are hard just now.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of IN A N CLIMATE IS gives INANCIALTIMES after the F. 'These' points at the newspaper carrying the puzzle, while the surface reads as the hard times of the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The newspaper printing this puzzle is meant by these, and economic hard times are financial times that are tough just now.

clue.text: Sea inlet where Jack goes in for diamonds

indicators.note: the card's letter goes into the middle of the other pieces, a container signal

parts.note: taken as written
J is the card abbreviation for jack
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card-game image: the jack is played where diamonds are wanted, beside a coastal inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for diamonds' reads like a card trade but simply gives FOR plus D, with J placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norwegian-style long narrow arm of the sea between steep cliffs is this kind of inlet.

clue.text: Clouds from high blue area gathered in north-east

indicators.note: the outer piece gathers the rest inside itself, a container signal

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

indicators.note: high in the sense of intoxicated or wild signals that the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A weather report: clouds from the high blue sky have gathered over the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like part of the sky description but is the anagram signal turning BLUE A into EBULA, which then sits between N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulae are interstellar clouds of gas and dust, so the plural astronomical sense matches.

clue.text: Who saw himself as winning girl over is pursuing church to become involved

indicators.note: to become involved means to be drawn into the middle of something, so one piece goes inside another
in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Susan is a girl's name

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so is comes after church

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic, a church
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone courting a girl again after she has been chasing the church gets tangled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winning' looks like part of the wordplay about courting, but it closes the definition: the youth of myth who thought himself irresistible. 'over' turns the girl's name round.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the youth fell in love with his own reflection, seeing himself as irresistibly attractive.

clue.text: Unnecessary one in 24 making way for German city

indicators.note: making way for means stepping aside so something else can take the place, a replacement signal

parts.note: the cross-reference points to the answer at 24 across, a word meaning letter
I is the Roman numeral for one
Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr

explanation.surface: Something deemed unnecessary has to make way for a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: The second I of the 24-across answer is replaced by ESSEN: IN plus ESSEN plus TIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not needed at all is unnecessary, the plain opposite of essential.

clue.text: Gain knowledge having evicted sailors in meadow

indicators.note: evicting means throwing out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: to learn is to gain knowledge
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: Someone learning about the countryside after turning the sailors out of a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a poetic word for an open grassy field or pasture.

clue.text: See 1
Working man invests pound in bank

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the bank takes the pound inside it

parts.note: a tier is a bank or row, as of seats
L, from libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: A labourer puts a pound into the bank as savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invests' and 'bank' push toward money; bank is a row, TIER, wrapped round L.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who lays roof or floor tiles is a working man.

clue.text: Perfect partner for the Tories?

parts.note: the ideal man a person hopes to marry, read playfully as a gentleman of the political right, where the Conservatives sit

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the ideal husband or partner, and the Tories are the party of the political right.

clue.text: Film director, back in boat, on downer for the Titanic!

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed below, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a boat
the ocean liner Titanic was sunk by an iceberg, shortened here to berg

explanation.surface: A film director sitting at the back of a boat, on a disaster like the Titanic's sinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Josef von Sternberg directed The Blue Angel; 'downer' is what brought the ship down.
explanation.definitionFit: Josef von Sternberg was an Austrian-American director of 1930s films.

clue.text: Chancellor steals to get return one pockets

indicators.note: to pocket is to put inside, so the number word holds the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: return means coming back, so the word for steals is read backwards

parts.note: robs means steals

explanation.surface: A finance minister is accused of stealing, pocketing money to make a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' suggests a tax return in this Treasury picture, but it signals the backwards reading. George Osborne was UK Chancellor of the Exchequer when this ran in 2012.
explanation.definitionFit: George Osborne served as Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer, the finance minister, from 2010.

clue.text: Roaming freely in a big way!

definitions.meaning: an escaped prisoner or animal on the loose is said to be free and roaming
read literally, the phrase means on a grand scale, in general or at length

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being free and unconfined, and also, read literally, being on a large scale.

clue.text: Husband in posh food shop generates capital

indicators.note: in signals that one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, an upmarket food shop

explanation.surface: A husband in an upmarket food shop runs up a sizeable sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money in this shopping picture; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi, and New Delhi within it, is the capital city of India.

clue.text: Bishop to grieve once more's not English one!

indicators.note: not means leaving out, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: to suffer again is to grieve once more; the apostrophe s is just is
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bishop is to grieve a second time, but this time he is not English.
explanation.walkthrough: SUFFER AGAIN loses its E and its I to leave SUFFRAGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A suffragan is a bishop who assists a diocesan bishop, without a see of his own.

clue.text: Made easier by Miliband to support info about Homeric work, these days irrelevant

indicators.note: in a down clue to support means to sit underneath, so the politician comes last
about means surrounding, so the word for info wraps round the epic

parts.note: a fact is a piece of information

indicators.note: irrelevant means not counting, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: the Iliad is Homer's epic poem
AD, anno Domini, means in the present era
at can mean by, as in standing at the door
Ed Miliband was leader of the UK Labour Party

explanation.surface: Ed Miliband is said to have brought facts about Homer's epic up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband led the UK Labour Party from 2010; 'these days' is the era abbreviation dropped from Homer's epic, and 'by' gives a short preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To facilitate is to make a process easier, so the past form means made easier.

clue.text: Some colliers are buried

indicators.note: some means only part of the word is used, so the answer sits inside it

explanation.surface: Some coal miners are underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The dead lie in their graves, so to be buried is to rest in the ground.

clue.text: Cloud over mischievous child showing leg

parts.note: the sky lowers, or lours, when it clouds over and turns dark
a limb is a mischievous child, as in limb of Satan

explanation.surface: A naughty child whose face darkens, showing a bit of leg.
explanation.walkthrough: LIMB for a rascal is old-fashioned British usage, short for limb of the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The leg is the lower limb of the human body.

clue.text: Revolutionary nut case lost in confusion

indicators.note: confusion means disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A revolutionary madman has gone missing amid the chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: The sans-culottes were the radical working-class revolutionaries of the French Revolution.

clue.text: First couple turned up with most elderly individual, an attractive person

indicators.note: turned up applies only to the opening two letters of the word for most elderly, which swap places

parts.note: the oldest is the most elderly
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: An elderly couple and the oldest person among them make an attractive pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' affects only the first couple of letters, which swap places; the definition is figurative, a magnet being what draws things to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetic mineral draws iron to it, and figuratively a centre of attraction is called this.

clue.text: Very talented author dies

parts.note: H. G. Wells was the English author of The War of the Worlds
killed means dies at another's hand

explanation.surface: A gifted writer has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone highly accomplished at a craft is very talented, with skill well developed.

clue.text: Czech saint is lord over unnamed Italian city

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the lord comes first

parts.note: Lud is an old form of lord, as in the exclamation Lud!

indicators.note: unnamed means without a name, so the N for name is dropped

parts.note: Milan is a city in northern Italy

explanation.surface: A Czech saint who is a lord ruling over an Italian city with no name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unnamed' removes N, the abbreviation for name, from the city; Lud is an archaic exclamation for lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Ludmila was a tenth-century Bohemian duchess and martyr venerated by Czechs.

clue.text: Short life one lost in Slough

indicators.note: lost means gone missing, so this letter is removed

parts.note: biog is the short form of biography, a life story
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A brief life of someone who went missing in Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is an English town west of London, but here it means a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a muddy swamp or marsh, the same as wet boggy ground.

clue.text: Fought Green, getting into bed with Liberal

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
raw means green, inexperienced

explanation.surface: A Green politician got into a coalition bed with a Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' and 'Liberal' suggest political parties, but green here means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: To brawl is to fight noisily and roughly, so fought fits in the past tense.

clue.text: Swimmer's ginger hairstyle

definitions.note: read as swimmer is, a fish

parts.note: ginger hair is red
a mullet is a hairstyle short at the front and long at the back

explanation.surface: A swimmer sports a ginger haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' looks like a person; it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a reddish fish of the Mediterranean, prized as food, so a creature that swims.

clue.text: Look to head north in UK boat

indicators.note: in signals that one piece goes inside another

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to aim is to direct one's gaze, to look

explanation.surface: Someone told to look northward for a boat in the UK.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to head north' reads the piece upwards; an umiak is an Inuit boat, so the UK setting misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: An umiak is an open Inuit boat of skins on a wooden frame.

clue.text: Passage has changed 1a 6a

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
FT is the usual abbreviation for the newspaper at 1 and 6 across

explanation.surface: A newspaper that has changed hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft is a vertical passage, as in a mine or lift.

clue.text: Best year for character in Stowe

parts.note: tops means the best, as in she's the tops

explanation.surface: The best year for a character in a novel by Stowe.
explanation.walkthrough: Stowe is also an English public school, but here it is Harriet Beecher Stowe.
explanation.definitionFit: Topsy is the slave girl in Harriet Beecher Stowe's novel Uncle Tom's Cabin.

clue.text: Letter from the front?

parts.note: reads as a soldier's message home from the war, but means a character standing at the start of a word or name

explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of a word or name stands at its front, as on a monogram.

clue.text: According to Sarkozy the wife makes the rules

parts.note: la is French for the, and Nicolas Sarkozy was French president

explanation.surface: In the Sarkozy household it is the wife who lays down the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Law is the body of rules a society enforces, so it means the rules collectively.

clue.text: Disreputable woman, fat, wearing blouse

indicators.note: the blouse is worn around the fat, a container signal

parts.note: a top is a garment such as a blouse
a roll is a fold of fat on the body

explanation.surface: An unkind picture of a woman with a roll of fat showing in her blouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat' looks like an adjective describing the woman but is a noun, a fold of flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollop is an old insult for a promiscuous or slovenly woman.

clue.text: British want time in week for withdrawal from ERM

parts.note: lack means want, as in for want of
Wednesday is a day of the week

explanation.surface: Britain's lack of time in a week led to the pound leaving the European exchange-rate system.
explanation.walkthrough: The ERM is the European Exchange Rate Mechanism, which the pound left on 16 September 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: The day in 1992 when sterling crashed out of the European currency mechanism is known by this name.
